companyDescription.title: Company Description
companyDescription.text:
A best-in-class city that attracts best-in-class talent, Philadelphia is an incredible place to build a career. From our thriving arts scene and rich history to our culture of passion and grit, there are countless reasons to love living and working here. With a workforce of over 30,000 people, and more than 1,000 different job categories, the City of Philadelphia offers boundless opportunities to make an impact.

As an employer, the City of Philadelphia values inclusion, integrity, innovation, empowerment, and hard work above all else. We offer a vibrant work environment, comprehensive health care and benefits, and the experience you need to grow and excel. If you’re interested in working with a passionate team of people who care about the future of Philadelphia, start here.

What We Offer:

Impact - The work you do here matters to millions.

Growth - Philadelphia is growing, why not grow with it?

Diversity & Inclusion - Find a career in a place where everyone belongs.

Benefits - We care about your well being.

The Office of Innovation & Technology (OIT) is the central IT agency for the City of Philadelphia headed by the Chief Information Officer (CIO). OIT oversees all major information and communications technology initiatives for the City of Philadelphia - increasing the effectiveness of the information technology infrastructure, where the services provided are advanced, optimized, and responsive to the needs of the City of Philadelphia’s businesses, residents, and visitors. OIT responsibilities include: identifying the most effective approach for implementing new information technology directions throughout city government; improving the value of the city’s technology assets and the return on the city’s technology investments; ensuring data security continuity; planning for continuing operations in the event of disruption of information technology or communications services; and supporting accountable, efficient and effective government across every city department, board, commission and agency.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Do you want to be at the forefront of CoP’s emerging cloud practice? We are seeking a junior engineer to support and expand our Cloud computing environment that has already provided great value to the City of Philadelphia by enabling modernization and optimization strategies. An ideal candidate is expected to operate independently, have a results-oriented mindset, and foster an environment of continuous improvement. A Cloud Engineer must possess strong interpersonal skills and regularly work with IT leaders and engineers in other departments.

This is primarily a cloud administration position focused on a hybrid cloud/on-premises environment across AWS GovCloud and Standard (Commercial) Cloud organizations. An ideal candidate will have a background in AWS, either professionally or managing their own accounts, and a solid basis in programming skills (ideally, Python). Although there is overlap with the skills and competencies associated with a DevOps role, this is not a DevOps role.

Essential Functions

  • Work in tandem with our architecture and engineering teams to identify and implement optimal cloud-based solutions
  • Manage a multi-account, multi-organization cloud environment in AWS
  • Plan and design cloud workloads to meet business needs with a focus on security
  • Document standard, best practices, and procedures across the environment
  • Automate infrastructure configuration and deployment throughout the development lifecycle
  • Manage and govern cloud environments. Monitor and optimize services to control costs and usage
  • Employ exceptional problem-solving skills, with the ability to see and solve issues before they affect business productivity
  • Stay current with industry trends and new services
  • Forecast cloud services costs for new workloads
  • Optimize existing workloads for cost and reliability

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
• AWS experience
  • Automating environments using Infrastructure as Code.
  • Familiarity with network technologies (VPCs, VPNs, Transit Gateways, Route53, Load Balancers, etc.)
  • Cloud architecture design (Well-Architected Framework)
  • Understanding of data and data integration concepts (SQL, data governance, enterprise patterns)
  • Python experience preferred.

Additional:  

  • Able to provide strong references successfully demonstrating such abilities and experience as defined above
  • Employment is contingent upon passing a CJIS background check
  • The employee must be a City of Philadelphia resident within six months of hire

Competencies, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Experience in AWS and architecture design.
  • Knowledge of design principles in cloud environments.
  • Familiarity with:
    • IAM and security in the Cloud;
    • cost optimization in AWS; and
    • networking.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to help project teams meet their goals while addressing enterprise concepts such as standards and security

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
The Technical Support Specialist works as part of a highly collaborative group that’s responsible for installation, configuration, and management of desktop and laptop computer systems. In addition to providing desktop support, you will participate in projects such as our ongoing Active Directory migration and multi-factor authentication rollout that require the Technical Support Specialist to learn new technologies and provide support for the creation of new processes for the team. The Technical Support Specialist will report to the Water Information Center Manager. This is a great opportunity for someone looking to increase their technical knowledge and abilities while at the same time using that knowledge to positively impact services for Philadelphia residents.

Essential Functions

Customer Relations:

  • Provide 1st tier support to customers
  • Answer help desk calls and create tickets in incident tracking system documenting support requests
  • Resolve assigned support tickets while keeping end user informed of the status of their request
  • Provide support to remote facilities using both remote tools and traveling to various facilities
  • Respond to end user inquiries by phone\email\chat
  • Create clear and detailed documentation
  • Explain technical issues to end users

Technical:

  • Troubleshoot issues with Windows operating systems, printers, and installed software
  • Configure laptops and desktops by installing operating system and updating needed drivers and firmware
  • Create and deploy images for laptops and desktops
  • Install software
  • Determine technical issues to escalate to tier 2 & tier 3 to support customers

  • Minimum 2 years of experience in a Desktop Support role

NOTE:  Microsoft Certified Professional (MCP) Certification (Windows 10) or an associate degree in Information Technology or Computer Technology can be substituted for any of the above experience

Skills:

  • A+ Certification

  • Excellent customer service skills
  • Excellent time-management skills

  • Ability to quickly learn new technologies

Knowledge Of:

  • MS Office and other PC software
  • Adobe Acrobat
  • Web Browsers (Chrome, IE, Firefox)
  • Windows desktop operating systems
  • Software licensing
  • Printers
  • Remote Desktop
  • VPN Software

Agency Description

The Office of Director of Finance was created by the Philadelphia Home Rule Charter, adopted by the electors of the City on April 17, 1951, to give the Mayor and the City government a principal officer responsible for the financial, accounting, and budgeting functions of the executive branch. The Director of Finance is thus the chief financial officer of the City, and all powers and duties concerning finances, accounting, and budgeting in the executive branch are directly or indirectly the Director's. The Director of Finance is also the Chairman of the Board of Pensions and Retirements and an ex-officio member of the board of various quasi-governmental agencies, including the Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority. The City of Philadelphia operates on a fiscal year between July 1st and June 30th.

 

The Office of the Director of Finance (Finance) is charged with overseeing the City’s financial, accounting, and budgetary functions, including: 

  • Establishing fiscal policy guidelines. 

  • Overseeing the City’s budget and financial management programs. 

  • Recording and accounting all City financial activities. 

Finance administers the City’s payroll activities and risk management functions, issues financial reports, and oversees expenditures and reports on all grants. Finance strives to ensure that the City maintains long-term fiscal stability while meeting its policy goals.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
Overview 

The Interface Lead will play a key role in modernizing, optimizing, managing, coordinating, and supporting system interfaces/integrations across OnePhilly. This position is responsible for leading the design, development, implementation, and maintenance of all system interfaces and data integrations between the core Oracle/ERP OnePhilly platform and external city systems, third-party vendors, pension boards, and financial institutions. This position requires strong technical and analytical capabilities, excellent communication skills, and the ability to quickly learn and adapt to new technologies. The Interface Lead will work directly with the Director, collaborating closely on interface strategy, documentation, testing, and ongoing improvements. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Leadership & Strategic Alignment: Collaborate directly with the Director of OnePhilly to prioritize interface needs, escalate critical issues, and provide ongoing updates on interface performance and project progress. 

  •  Integration Strategy & Architecture: Define and execute the interface development strategy, ensuring integrations align with City architectural standards, data security policies, and the overarching OnePhilly project roadmap. 

  • End-to-End Delivery: Lead the full lifecycle of data interfaces, including requirements gathering, data mapping, technical specification design, building, testing, and deployment. 

  • Stakeholder & Vendor Coordination: Serve as the primary technical point of contact for external benefit vendors, banks, vendors, and 50+ city operating departments to facilitate seamless data exchange. 

  • Quality Assurance & Testing: Formulate strict testing protocols (Unit, System Integration, and User Acceptance Testing) to ensure HR, OTL, payroll, pension, and benefit transactions process with 100% data integrity. 

  • Monitoring & Incident Management: Oversee daily interface processing, error-handling protocols, and performance tuning. Quickly diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve critical data mismatches or interface failures. 

  • Compliance & Security: Ensure all inbound and outbound file transfers (SFTP, Direct Access, flat files) comply with modern data security policies, PII regulations, and strict audit requirements. 

  • Team Leadership: Provide guidance and mentorship to developers, data analysts, and business analysts working on data integrations. 

Required Skills & Qualifications 

  • Strong technical and analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex data and system interactions 

  • Demonstrated ability to learn quickly and adapt to new software, tools, and technologies. 

  • Experience with interface testing, troubleshooting, and documentation. 

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. 

  • High attention to detail and strong organizational skills. 

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. 

  • Familiarity with system integrations, data mapping, or workflow design is a plus 

  • Expertise with Windows MS Office suite is a must.

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
Education and Experience: 

Completion of a Bachelor’s Degree Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Data Analytics,  or a closely related field. 

Five years of progressively responsible experience supporting, developing, testing, or managing enterprise system interfaces and data integrations. 

At least two years of experience coordinating technical work, or providing functional or technical guidance to developers, analysts, vendors, or project teams.
